title: Frontend mid scenario memory leak debug
topic: Frontend mid scenario memory leak debug
question: Users report the tab gets slower and slower the longer they leave your app open, and eventually the browser tab crashes. How would you track this down?
idealAnswer:
Use the browser's memory profiler to take heap snapshots at different points in time and compare them (e.g. after navigating between views repeatedly) to see which object types keep growing

Look for classic leak sources: event listeners added on mount but never removed on unmount, timers/intervals not cleared, and subscriptions (WebSocket, observers) not torn down when a component unmounts

Check for detached DOM nodes, elements removed from the visible tree but still referenced by a closure or a global variable, which prevents garbage collection

Check for growing caches or arrays that accumulate data across navigations without ever being cleared, e.g. an in-memory log or cache with no eviction policy

Reproduce deliberately by navigating between the same two views many times and watching whether memory climbs monotonically, versus climbing and settling, which narrows down whether it's a true leak or just normal variance
